# `js/comment-type`

**Comments are written in the allowed types**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:js/taste` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `types` |
| **Fix** | `auto` — `codelaw fix` applies it; it never changes what the code does (a comment says the same in any type, so rewriting it changes no code; a directive, a pragma and a comment between two pieces of code on one line are left alone) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `tslint/comment-type` |

## What it checks

A comment is written in one of the `types` the project allows — by default `singleline` and `doc`, so a plain `/* … */` block is reported — and any other comment is rewritten as the first allowed type that can hold it: a block as `//` lines (a comment with code after it on its line puts the code on the next line), a run of `//` lines as one block, a doc comment as a plain block. Left alone: directives and pragmas (`/// <reference>`, `// @ts-…`, `/* eslint-… */`, `/*! licence */`, `/*#__PURE__*/`, `//# sourceMappingURL`), a comment in JSX braces, a block with code on both sides of it on its line (`f(/* x */ 1)`), and a `//` comment whose text holds `*/`. TSLint's `jsdoc` type is read as `doc`.

**Why:** One comment style per codebase is read faster, and a block comment that holds no code is a line comment in a longer coat.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:js/taste` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/taste"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/comment-type" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `types` | `string[]` | `["singleline", "doc"]` | the comment types the project writes: `singleline` (`//`), `multiline` (`/* */`) and `doc` (`/** */`, also spelt `jsdoc`) |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."js/comment-type"]
severity = "error"

[rules."js/comment-type".options]
types = ["singleline", "doc"]
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"js/comment-type" = { severity = "error", options = { types = ["singleline", "doc"] } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `types`

*string[]* · default `["singleline", "doc"]`

the comment types the project writes: `singleline` (`//`), `multiline` (`/* */`) and `doc` (`/** */`, also spelt `jsdoc`)

```toml
[rules."js/comment-type".options]
types = ["singleline", "doc"]
```

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/comment-type" = { options = { types = ["singleline", "doc"] } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/comment-type" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/comment-type" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/comment-type" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/comment-type" = { severity = "warn", options = { types = ["singleline", "doc"] } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/comment-type": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"types": ["singleline", "doc"]}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/comment-type: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/comment-type expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/comment-type --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/comment-type       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/comment-type  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>   # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
/* total price with tax */
const total = price * 1.2;
```

#### Do

```js
// total price with tax
const total = price * 1.2;
```

#### Fixed

```js
// total price with tax
const total = price * 1.2;
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
/* total price with tax */
const total = price * 1.2;
```

#### Do

```jsx
// total price with tax
const total = price * 1.2;
```

#### Fixed

```jsx
// total price with tax
const total = price * 1.2;
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
/* total price with tax */
const total = price * 1.2;
```

#### Do

```ts
// total price with tax
const total = price * 1.2;
```

#### Fixed

```ts
// total price with tax
const total = price * 1.2;
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
/* total price with tax */
const total = price * 1.2;
```

#### Do

```tsx
// total price with tax
const total = price * 1.2;
```

#### Fixed

```tsx
// total price with tax
const total = price * 1.2;
```
